candidate_diffs.title: Store small obligation dependency lists inline
candidate_diffs.head: 1847fd8421419530078a59c7d30e4957fb633527
candidate_diffs.historical_body:
Store up to two obligation dependency indices inline with `SmallVec`. Most lists are small, so this avoids a separate allocation while preserving their order and allowing larger lists to spill to the heap.

In isolation against #81, full-check instruction counts fell 0.09% for bitmaps and 0.13% for syn. Unchanged and patched incremental checks changed little.

candidate_diffs.title: Reduce fast-rejection overhead for single generic arguments
candidate_diffs.head: aa32a253490d9f90be2944acda4b461df72744a6
candidate_diffs.historical_body:
Special-case single generic arguments in fast rejection, return early for identical arguments, and keep recursive structural checks out of line. This reduces the setup needed for common trait-candidate comparisons.

Against #98, compiler instruction counts fell 2.18% across a four-crate rustc-perf Check/Debug sample, mostly from bitmaps (7.6–8.4%). Reductions were 0.12% for Ruff's `ty_python_semantic` and 0.18% for `uv-resolver`. Wall-time results varied across runs.

candidate_diffs.title: Reduce trait and dataflow overhead
candidate_diffs.head: 827d0887cd34362c3665ffe77bdcd62dd9a8ab6c
candidate_diffs.historical_body:
Prune coherence checks for impls with incompatible const arguments. Skip unchanged well-formedness normalization, compare sizedness trait IDs directly, inline predicate reuse checks, and reuse borrow-checking allocations.

Against #103, the four-crate Check/Debug suite uses 3.255% fewer instructions in ABBA and 3.259% fewer in BAAB (64 Cachegrind profiles on x86_64). All eight cases improve. The 5,937 UI tests and affected unit tests pass.

Ruff's `ty_python_semantic` uses 0.990% fewer instructions and `uv-resolver` uses 1.183% fewer across 16 Cachegrind profiles, with identical metadata and diagnostics. Linux and macOS regression checks pass. CodSpeed reports no significant change across all 22 benchmarks. The geometric mean of case mean times falls only 0.13–0.20% against two runs of #103.

candidate_diffs.title: Merge equivalent functions before LLVM inlining
candidate_diffs.head: 5ea69eb1cbc4025cdd1dcc5c13c91e4e8a31a608
candidate_diffs.historical_body:
Run LLVM's function-merging pass before inlining so equivalent bodies share the remaining optimization work. This applies to optimized prelink pipelines with function merging enabled and no PGO, sanitizers, coverage, or plugins.

ARM64 Release comparisons with prebuilt dependencies reduced compilation time by [1.35% for `codex-protocol`](https://github.com/astral-sh/ohm-rust/actions/runs/33926482373) and [0.48% for `uv-resolver`](https://github.com/astral-sh/ohm-rust/actions/runs/33923879209). These compared `66c1849` against #107 (`4627d215`), using the system allocator without PGO/BOLT. The Check and unoptimized Debug cases in CodSpeed CI do not exercise this pass.

candidate_diffs.title: Skip redundant per-body work in Rust analysis
candidate_diffs.head: bc78967e759f8bef0708a888d5e73c51ecf4b267
candidate_diffs.historical_body:
Reuse the constraint graph from region SCC computation during borrow checking. We also assign known parameter types directly and skip type-checker fallback, writeback, loop diagnostics, and reachability work when it cannot affect the result.

Keep the three borrow-checker analyses on independent worklists, so one that needs more iterations cannot force the others to repeat their work. This gives up some small gains from sharing their worklist.

Across eight rustc-perf Check/Full workloads, median compiler instruction counts fell by 0.1–1.8% versus the parent on x86-64 Linux (Cachegrind, two samples per compiler). This targeted screen covers the two previous regressions above 1% and six other workloads.

candidate_diffs.title: Reuse the source checksum buffer across files
candidate_diffs.head: 3b8f3390a2feb4e13a9805d33ac512568146d602
candidate_diffs.historical_body:
Reuse a lazily allocated 64 KiB buffer across source checksums in a freshness scan. Previously, each uncached file allocated its own 16 KiB buffer. Cache hits and early stale-file exits still avoid allocation.

On an Apple M5 Max, warm-corpus benchmarks using Ruff, uv, and Codex checksum inputs reduced isolated open/read/hash time by 6.7–9.5%. Full Cargo check/Clippy comparisons were mixed, from 1.67% faster to 0.87% slower, so they do not establish a whole-command speedup. Those comparisons used local release builds without PGO and eight samples per variant in ABBA/BAAB order.

candidate_diffs.title: Port used-underscore name prefilters
candidate_diffs.head: 7a06fab3512a6fbed91fa101bb11195687e85ec5
candidate_diffs.patch_format: preserved GitHub complete one-file unified hunk; exact record also bound
candidate_diffs.historical_body:
Check for a single leading underscore before running the more expensive context checks in `used_underscore_binding` and `used_underscore_items`.

Ordinary names now skip macro, desugaring, and automatically-derived checks. The existing exclusions still apply to names that can produce a diagnostic.

candidate_diffs.title: Avoid redundant formatter configuration ancestor walks
candidate_diffs.head: a29f0e3d64ef2eb466e6034617d2132c4c613915
candidate_diffs.patch_format: preserved GitHub complete one-file unified hunk; exact record also bound
candidate_diffs.historical_body:
Stop walking configuration ancestors when we reach a directory already visited for the same workspace snapshot. Previously, each source directory repeated the remaining walk to the root.

Nearest-configuration precedence and detection of newly created configuration files are unchanged.
